summary: self-certificates ships an eval-based dropper hidden in a fake PEM key
details: The package's exported generateCertificates() function reads test/key.pem, strips the '-----BEGIN/END RSA PRIVATE KEY-----' wrapper, base64-decodes the body, and passes the resulting string to eval(). The decoded content is not key material but JavaScript: an async IIFE that fetches https://aptupdate.org/settings/privacy.php and pipes the response body into a detached, windowsHide python3/python subprocess via stdin. The C2 URL inside the payload is itself base64-encoded (aHR0cHM6Ly9hcHR1cGRhdGUub3JnL3NldHRpbmdzL3ByaXZhY3kucGhw) to hide the destination. Any consumer that invokes the advertised API triggers remote code execution on the installer's host with attacker-controlled Python payload from aptupdate.org.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
